content.comment_body: Hello everyone, I'm new to PLC systems and have a project where I need to change a standard on/off switch to a push button with a delay-off feature. After doing some research, I found I could use a [company_name] [product_name] instead of traditional relay timer switches. Unfortunately, I'm unsure how to proceed with programming and installation. Any help would be appreciated!
Which [product_name] do you have? Is it a 230V version or something else? If different, does it have relay outputs?

Thank you for following up. I'm working with the 230V [product_name], and I also have the [product_name] Power with 24V DC output, plus relay output. The screenshot you shared—is it ladder logic or another programming language? I want the timer to have about a 45-minute delay. Thanks again.
The programming language in the screenshot is called FBD. You can set the delay to 45 minutes as well.
The image may help clarify the wiring setup. The phase used for the button and the [product_name]'s power supply should be the same.

analysis.insight_summary: A user is having difficulty moving from relay-based timers to programmable controls using the [company_name] [product_name] platform, especially with programming timer functions and wiring. Community responses focus on specifying device models, identifying programming languages, and providing practical wiring advice.
analysis.user_expectations: The user is looking for easy ways to set up a delay-off function using [product_name], hoping for instructions that guide both programming and hardware setup, with clear explanations and beginner-friendly resources.
